def: The slope that chord slopes settle to as the step shrinks to zero: how fast a function's output changes per unit change in its input.
An estimate of a derivative from function values at nearby points, such as (f(x+h) - f(x-h)) / 2h.
The rule that the derivative of a composed function is the product of the local derivatives along the chain.
The derivative of a function of several variables with respect to one of them, holding the others fixed.
The vector of all partial derivatives of a scalar function; it points in the direction of steepest ascent and has the shape of the parameters.
The slope of a function along a chosen unit direction, equal to the dot product of the gradient with that direction.
The (m, n) matrix of partial derivatives of an m-vector function of an n-vector, the best linear approximation of the function near a point.
Testing an analytic gradient against finite differences, entry by entry, using relative error in float64.
A valid slope to use at a kink such as ReLU at zero, where the ordinary derivative does not exist.
The matrix of second partial derivatives, describing the curvature of a function in every direction.
The collapse of a gradient towards zero when it passes back through many layers whose local derivatives are below one.
